subject: Share one segmented product across three portable database branch-page cases
claim: The three existing branch-page Main functions execute in one portable bundle, sharing 15 library modules and reducing declared source visits from 48 to 19. Fresh Windows construction, packaging, and behavior passed in 52110 ms. Focused development passes with three logical cases and one execution on both hosts, with unchanged warm runs of 3353 ms on Windows and 8108 ms on Debian. The portable WVB bytes match across hosts. Qualification retains 57 cases in 52 steps; development retains 53 cases in 45 executions.

limitations: The 210-second separate-product baseline is incomplete, with only its first two cases recorded as passed. It is not an exact three-case completion-time comparison. The baseline bound terminated the entire active process tree.

The first diagnostic invocations rejected a Windows resource path and noncanonical source dependency order; both were corrected before the successful construction, without changing runtime semantics or bounds.

Cold means fresh test products and construction checkpoints with retained qualified bootstrap tools, not a clean machine. Full database qualification and complete paired-host repository qualification were not run.

Windows development, Debian focused qualification, and routing verification ran concurrently on the same physical host; these elapsed times are diagnostic single observations. The initial Windows separate-product baseline and successful 52110 ms bundle construction were sequential.
Windows warm time is 3353 ms end to end (2950 ms owner timing); Debian warm is 8108 ms (7000 ms coarse shell timing). Debian remains above the five-second focused target.
Native runtime and image limits were unchanged. Peak memory was not measured.

The old individual projects remain available for partial development selections; the bundle is selected only when all three declared members are selected. Existing rejection and boundary cases remain inside the original test functions.
